sources.title: Exact repository interview question and Batch 0033 frozen source boundary

claims.text: The source preserves only the single-thread true/false rate-limiter task; window/accounting/clock/boundary details are answer-side contracts.
Under the declared sliding-window admission contract, an ordered deque evicts expired successful admissions, rejects at capacity and otherwise appends now.
The exact Java implementation passes deterministic capacity, rejection, boundary, burst, clock-regression and invalid-configuration tests.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS sliding-window accepted-only exact-boundary burst regression invalid-config
checks: rejected calls at 300/999ms then call at 1000ms
two calls at same timestamp with max=2 then third call

boundary_tests.case: rejected calls at 300/999ms then call at 1000ms
boundary_tests.expected: rejections consume no capacity; 0ms expires; 1000ms accepted

boundary_tests.case: two calls at same timestamp with max=2 then third call

findings: The repository source preserves a single-thread true/false rate-limiter coding task but does not preserve the window algorithm, time units, attempt-versus-admission accounting, clock API or exact boundary semantics.

The candidate labels sliding-window, accepted-only accounting, non-negative non-decreasing injected time, the half-open window and rejected-attempt behavior as answer-side contracts rather than recovered facts.
The exact fenced Java equals the saved fixture and passes capacity, rejection, exact-boundary expiry, same-timestamp burst, clock-regression and invalid-configuration checks under JDK 21.

The queue invariant, amortized O(1) argument, O(maxCalls) space bound, single-thread limitation, and fixed-window/token-bucket/leaky-bucket variants are directly tied to this problem without fabricated project claims.
